content: All individuals and groups are entitled to access evidence-based information regarding sexual and reproductive health (SRH), including information on safe abortion and post-abortion care. This right is recognized under international human rights frameworks, such as the International Covenant on Economic, Social, and Cultural Rights (ICESCR), as outlined in General Comment No. 22 (2016). Information on SRH, including safe abortion and post-abortion care, must be provided in accessible formats to ensure inclusivity, particularly for women and girls with disabilities, as emphasized in the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD) General Comment No. 3 (2016). States have an obligation to ensure the free flow of health information, including information on abortion, without interference based on moral or other grounds. This principle is supported by the United Nations Working Group on the issue of discrimination against women in law and practice (2016). States are required to ensure affordable access to essential medicines, as stated in General Comment No. 25 (2020) of the ICESCR. This includes preventing unreasonably high costs for such medicines and ensuring that women have access to up-to-date scientific technologies necessary for their health, including contraception and abortion medication. States must guarantee access to modern and safe forms of contraception, including emergency contraception, abortion medication, assisted reproductive technologies, and other sexual and reproductive health goods and services. These must be provided on the basis of non-discrimination and equality, as outlined in General Comment No. 25 (2020) of the ICESCR. Forced or coerced abortion on women with disabilities is a violation of their rights, including their right to retain fertility on an equal basis with others. Such practices constitute a form of discrimination against persons with disabilities, as highlighted in CRPD General Comment No. 6 (2018) and the Special Rapporteur on torture and other cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment or punishment (2008). Non-consensual abortion, even when conducted under lawful decision-making processes by a legal guardian, can amount to torture or ill-treatment. This is particularly true when the procedure is aimed at correcting or alleviating disability, as noted by the Special Rapporteur on the right to health (2009). States must respect the sexual and reproductive health and rights of women and girls with disabilities. This includes ensuring that SRH services are provided in accessible formats and prohibiting discriminatory denial of such services. These obligations are outlined in CRPD General Comment No. 6 (2018) and other international human rights instruments.
